Wait, when the cross center was at (9,24), the cross's horizontal arm at row 9 covered cols 13-35, and the vertical arm at col 24 covered rows -2..20. Maybe the cross's pixels covered them in the rendering, and the segmentation merged them... no, the segmentation is per-color; charcoal is charcoal.

Maybe they got overwritten by the cross's yellow pixels? No... the cross's center is at (9,24) with a white core; the vertical arm at col 24 is yellow at rows 0-8 and 10-20; the horizontal arm at row 9 is yellow at cols 13-23 and 25-35. So the square's frame pixels (8,24) and (10,24) — row 8 col 24 is on the vertical arm → yellow. (9,23),(9,25) are on the horizontal arm → yellow. So when the cross center is on the square's center, the cross's arms cover the top/bottom/left/right frame pixels, and only the 4 corners remain visible as charcoal. Now that the cross has moved away, those 4 pixels are... back to charcoal? That would mean they were never destroyed — they're just hidden under the cross. But the center pixel (9,24) was white (the core) — and now it's gone (absorbed).
So: collection = the square's center pixel is consumed when the cross center passes over it; the frame pixels remain (temporarily hidden by the cross). The shattered square remains as a 3x3 charcoal frame with an empty center.
OK, so the "collected" square leaves a hollow frame. No problem.

The square's center is (17,15); the cross center is (18,15) — 1px off. If collection is only via center overlap, it won't be collected. Let's test: move to (18,15) and check whether the (17,15) square got collected.
Actually wait — the square's center (17,15) is 1px from the cross center (18,15). The cross's vertical arm passes through (17,15) (col 15, rows 7-29). If the arm's passage collects it, it'll be collected. Let's test.
